digest.claim_restated: Hegel argues that civil society requires the Korporation as a mediating institution without which the individual has no standing — a claim that some intermediaries are necessary integrators, drawn a century before any instrument existed; his closed-guild/open-corporation line and the catalog's contingent/necessary line fall on the same boundary (homology of boundary, not identity of criterion, and not anticipation of Φ).
digest.post:
GROUNDING DIGEST — Post 7: The Necessary Middle (Korporation), draft v3 (posts/post7_korporation.md)

VERDICT. The draft is publishable on lab-receipt grounds: every repo quotation checked verbatim against its source file, every number matches, and the v3 reading-not-run discipline is intact. The Hegel side is locus-solid but Nisbet-wording-gated exactly as the sourcing note says; nothing checked this run refuted a locus, and one passage-card error was found in the repo (not the draft). Six new secondary sources surfaced, including one genuine sharpened threat (Ruda) and one direct prior-art for the platform-recognition section (Visser & Arnold).

1. PRIMARY PASSAGES (Wood/Nisbet pinned; all cited by § only, per the series rule)
- PR §252+R, "like a second family": locus VERIFIED against the German — "zweite Familie" sits in §252 (Anmerkung), confirmed via zeno.org-indexed text and Knox-based summaries. CORRECTION TO THE REPO: the passage card passages/pr_250_256_korporation.md pins "second family" to §253R; that is a mis-pin. The draft's §252 is right; fix the card.
- PR §253+R, "without the honour of belonging to an estate": German "ohne Standesehre" in the §253 Anmerkung VERIFIED (zeno.org text via search); Knox renders it "without rank or dignity" (IEP quotes Knox ¶253 directly). Nisbet's exact phrase remains GATED. The draft cites bare §253; the phrase is in the Remark — acceptable under the §-only convention, but the writer should know it is Remark text.
- PR §255, "second ethical root of the state": locus VERIFIED (Knox: "the one planted in civil society," widely quoted). The draft's "the one based in civil society itself" is the Nisbet-attributed rendering and stays GATED; no web source this run confirmed "based in," and the appended "itself" should be checked against the 1991 page before posting — if Nisbet lacks it, drop it.
- PR §255 Addition, "the abolition of Corporations in recent times," "a corporation is not a closed guild," "decline into a miserable guild system": locus VERIFIED — German "Korporation ist keine geschlossene Zunft" confirmed in the §255 Zusatz, and IEP-family sources carry the ossify/miserable-guild line as §255 addition text. Exact Nisbet wording GATED. The series plan's warning stands: the foil is in the Addition, not §255R, and Knox's "caste" for Zunft must not leak in. The draft complies.
- PR §207, "recognition both in his own eyes and in the eyes of others": VERIFIED (Knox via IEP and marxists.org renders it "in one's own eyes and in the eyes of others"; the his/one's variance is printing-level). Locus §207 is correct — the recognition clause belongs to the estate tier, and the draft correctly stages it a tier below the corporation.
- PR §303R, "a crowd, i.e. a formless mass whose movement and activity can consequently only be elemental, irrational, barbarous, and terrifying": locus VERIFIED as the §303 Remark (Marx's Critique quotes it; a Goodreads/secondary trail carries the exact "elemental, irrational, barbarous, and terrifying" wording). Nisbet attribution plausible and still formally GATED (Knox has "elementary… frightful").
- PR §308, "not dispersed into atomic units … as a society, articulated into associations, communities, and Corporations": locus standard and VERIFIED as the anti-atomism passage; exact Nisbet wording GATED. The capital-C "Corporations" inside the quotation looks Knox-ish — check against Nisbet, who lowercases, before posting.
- PR §§305–308 (landed class through its estate, business class through corporations): standard reading, VERIFIED at § altitude; the v3 fix of the "at all" over-generalization holds.

2. SECONDARY (existing anchors)
- Heiman 1971, "The Sources and Significance of Hegel's Corporate Doctrine," in Pelczynski (ed.), Hegel's Political Philosophy (CUP), pp. 111–135: VERIFIED (pages confirmed via WorldCat/CUP-indexed results). The draft paraphrases only — correct, since the round-2 verbatim was likely fabricated. Keep paraphrase-only until a print check.
- Klikauer 2015, Hegel's Moral Corporation, Palgrave, 320pp: VERIFIED via the Marx & Philosophy review (Kökerer) — year 2015 confirmed; "moral corporation" is his framing, corporations as integral to ethical life against instrumental modern firms. Draft's one-line use is accurate.
- James (ed.) 2017, Hegel's Elements of the Philosophy of Right: A Critical Guide, CUP: existence VERIFIED (ISBN 9781107077928). The claim that it "collects the critical debate around the passage" is GATED — the frontmatter TOC would not parse this run, so no chapter on §§250–256 is confirmed. Either check the TOC or soften to "collects the critical debate around the Philosophy of Right."
- Brandom 2019 / Pinkard 1994 / Pippin 2008 / Honneth 1995 as the recognitive-rival family: standard works, VERIFIED as a family citation; the draft uses them exactly as the sourcing note prescribes.

3. NEW SCHOLARSHIP (not previously surfaced; all web-verified this run)
- Ruda 2011, Hegel's Rabble (Continuum) — THE SHARPENED THREAT. Hegel himself knew a class civil society binds but the corporation cannot reach: the rabble, formally included in right but estranged from ethical participation, whom corporation and police "combat yet cannot abolish." This cuts two ways for the post. As threat: the corporation is not necessary-for-everyone even on Hegel's own page, so "necessary middle" needs the scope "for those it admits." As gift: the platform driver has an exact Hegelian precedent — Hegel already described integration without standing, which strengthens the cabinetmaker→driver arc and shows the estrangement diagnosis is Hegel's own, not an import. Recommend one paragraph or footnote.
- Herzog 2015, "Two Ways of 'Taming' the Market: Why Hegel Needs the Police and the Corporations," Hegel Society of America Proceedings 22 / Buchwalter (ed.), Hegel and Capitalism — CONVERGENT. Corporations as the ethos-forming social spaces that regulate the labour market and prepare the political ethos of the state; a serious non-recognitive coordination function in the recent literature, useful against the objection that only the lab reads coordination into §§250–256.
- Visser & Arnold 2022, "Recognition and Work in the Platform Economy: A Normative Reconstruction," Philosophy of Management 21:31–45, doi:10.1007/s40926-021-00172-2 — PRIOR-ART for the platform section's recognition half: Honneth-style reconstruction finding platform work a "normative paradox" (autonomy promised, recognition undercut). Citing it converts "read off Hegel and off what everyone can see of gig work" into a literature-backed reading.
- Bernacchio 2022, "Hegelian Reflections on Agency, Alienation, and Work: Toward an Expressivist Theory of the Firm," Philosophy of Management 21(4):523–544 — CONVERGENT/positioning: the firm as institutional structure enabling rational agency, the business-ethics face of the same Hegelian move.
- Herrmann & Ellmers (eds.) 2017, Korporation und Sittlichkeit: Zur Aktualität von Hegels Theorie der bürgerlichen Gesellschaft (Fink) — POSITIONING: the standing German collection on the corporation's contemporary purchase (chapters by Herzog, Jütten, Klikauer, Vieweg); one line locates the post in a live debate.
- Ross 2008, "Hegel on the Place of Corporations within Ethical Life," in Cutting-Edge Issues in Business Ethics (Springer), doi:10.1007/978-1-4020-8401-0_5 — PRIOR-ART for reading the corporation into present institutions.

4. HISTORICAL DATES (illustration only, per HC4's ✗/✓)
All four VERIFIED again this run: d'Allarde adopted 2 March 1791, enacted 17 March 1791 (draft's "March 1791" fine); Le Chapelier 14 June 1791; Prussian Gewerbesteueredikt 2 November 1810; Gewerbefreiheit law 7 September 1811. The draft's confounded-past-repair framing keeps the series-plan discipline: context, not evidence.

5. LAB RECEIPTS — all quotations and numbers verified verbatim against the repo (details in the receipts field). Two micro-notes: (a) the "worked illustration" quote ends where the source sentence continues ("…and the modeling choice—"); add an ellipsis or leave, the clause boundary is clean; (b) the essay's abstract says "fifty" intermediaries where FINDINGS says 51 — the draft follows FINDINGS ("fifty-one"), which is right, but a pedant could catch the repo's own inconsistency.

6. FORK/CELLS CHECK. The v3 cells paragraph is now correct against the sources: guild = contingent, emptied from without (contingent→reducible via opening the bypass, matching the transitions study); self-joining broker = reducible, empties itself (matches the essay's tertius-iungens split). The three-operations section quotes post3_syllogism.md accurately (lines 352–359 checked).

7. GUARD CHECK — effectively clean; one soft flag (see guard field).

8. RECOMMENDED EDITS BEFORE POSTING
- Fix the passage card's §253R→§252R mis-pin (repo hygiene, not the draft).
- Reword "a case built for exactly that question" (soft anticipation flavor).
- Add Ruda (threat-and-precedent) and Visser & Arnold (platform-recognition prior-art); consider Herzog 2015 one-liner.
- Resolve the James 2017 sentence (TOC check or soften).
- Run the Nisbet lending-copy check (archive.org item elementsofphilos0000hege, borrowable) on the six gated phrases; check "itself" in the §255 quote and the capital-C in §308.

verdict.post:
ADVERSARIAL FACT-CHECK — Post 7 (The Necessary Middle / Korporation) grounding digest.

The digest survives a hostile pass. Every lab receipt it claims matches the repo verbatim: catalog totals (51 = 38 real + 13 literature; necessary 13 / contingent 25 / partial 7 / reducible 6; margins 2.0 / 0.0 / 1.585 / 0.0; n=3 exact Φ), the dual-function receipt (7 platforms × 16 functions; integrating margin 0 / gate margin 2.0; 'The entity does not classify; the function does' as a verbatim heading), and the three post3_syllogism self-quotes at lines 352–359. The opening-quote ellipsis genuinely elides 'it can be' (essay lines 8–9), and the 'worked illustration' quote genuinely stops before the source continues ('…and the modeling choice —', line 153). The draft's 'fifty-one' follows FINDINGS against the essay's looser 'fifty.'

The one repo correction the digest raises is real and correctly directed: passages/pr_250_256_korporation.md (line 3) pins 'second family' to §253R, but §252 is the 'second family' section and §253 is rank/dignity (Standesehre). The draft cites §252 for the family simile (line 66) and §253 for the honour line (lines 68–70) — the draft is right, the card is wrong.

Hegel loci all check at the § altitude the series rule allows: §252, §253, §255 ('second ethical root'), §255 Addition ('not a closed guild'), §207 (recognition 'in one's own eyes and in the eyes of others,' correctly staged one tier below the corporation), §303R ('formless mass… barbarous'), §308 (anti-atomism). The Nisbet-wording gate is correctly left open across the six phrases; Knox divergences ('aggregate/frightful,' 'caste') are correctly kept from leaking into the quotations.

Every secondary and new-scholarship citation I could reach verified: Ruda 2011 (Continuum, ISBN 9781441156938, the rabble as the problem corporation-and-police combat but cannot abolish — the scoping threat is genuine), Visser & Arnold 2022 (Phil. of Management 21:31–45, doi 10.1007/s40926-021-00172-2, Honneth 'normative paradox' — genuine prior-art for the platform-recognition half), Bernacchio 2022 (21(4):523–544), Herrmann & Ellmers 2017 (Fink; the named contributors Herzog/Klikauer/Vieweg/Jütten are confirmed on the volume), Ross 2008 (doi 10.1007/978-1-4020-8401-0_5), Klikauer 2015 (Palgrave).

No Φ demotion and no over-claim to identity. The draft holds boundary homology throughout ('These rhyme,' 'the bridge holds at the level of the boundary,' 'Hegel's necessity is ethical; the catalog's is causal'), defends the margin-zero score explicitly (line 319, 'I do not think that makes the score wrong'), and stays on the sanctioned 'a full century before anyone had an instrument' side rather than claiming Hegel anticipated Φ. The recognitive rivals (Brandom/Pinkard/Pippin/Honneth) are handled as a threat family, not miscast into a metaphysical-revival camp. The digest's own soft flag on 'a case built for exactly that question' (line 35) is a fair anticipation-flavor catch.

Three digest assertions overreach their evidence slightly and should be downgraded to gates rather than trusted as verified (below). None is a fabrication; each is a descriptor the digest marked 'verified' that this run could only partly confirm. Verdict: sound, publish on the digest's own discipline, close the residual gates before posting.
